I looked into whether applying the cached settings on server start could "clobber" a newer update received via gossip. The answer is no, but we should make this clearer/less prone to rot. I think the way to go is to pass the `initialSettingsKVs` to this method:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9b8526454df4b9e43bb9d5e7005010f44cb4edac/pkg/server/server.go#L1574

That method sets up the gossip-based settings listener. By putting this method in charge of applying the initial cache to the settings before consulting gossip for updates, proper sequencing is "obvious".

Additionally, we should move that call above to the place where your PR currently populates the cache, https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9b8526454df4b9e43bb9d5e7005010f44cb4edac/pkg/server/server.go#L1419

That way we continue to make sure that the settings are applied as early as possible in the start sequence. We will start the settings gossip event loop earlier, but that is not an issue.

Btw, you're catching some merge conflicts with some simplifications @irfansharif is landing these days, they shouldn't be substantial.

If I'm passing initial settings to
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9b8526454df4b9e43bb9d5e7005010f44cb4edac/pkg/server/server.go#L1574

I don't think we require 
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9b8526454df4b9e43bb9d5e7005010f44cb4edac/pkg/server/server.go#L1419

Moreover, I did not know if I should move `refreshSettings` above, and so I populated the initial settings before. Just confirming that we're on the same page.

Looks like we're trying to hit the admin UI (`/_status/gossip/local`) shortly after the cluster starts up and we hit this error. This is an indication that the server has not received an updated version of the cluster settings, otherwise is would be aware that `server.remote_debugging.mode` was set to `'any'` [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/c433a62d7dedb94ffaf00bd679714636859217fa/pkg/cmd/roachprod/install/cockroach.go#L326).

One thing we see in the logs from this node is that:
```
W200424 07:42:12.970613 143 server/node.go:670  [n1] [n1,s1]: unable to compute metrics: [n1,s1]: system config not yet available
```
fires a few times after:
```
I200424 07:41:42.969732 24 server/server.go:1419  [n1] starting http server at [::]:26258 (use: 10.128.0.76:26258)
I200424 07:41:49.029579 99 gossip/gossip.go:1538  [n1] node has connected to cluster via gossip
```

Yes, that sounds reasonable. The settings are not persisted on the node, so we're always running with the default settings for a little bit of time even after signaling readiness.

Something we could do here is to wait until a system config has been ingested before returning from `.Start` (in the non-init case). But we're also phasing out this use of Gossip, so this will rot quickly, and the new system will use higher-level primitives. For now, seems best to add a retry or sleep to the test.

We cannot indiscriminately block on receiving the settings before signaling ready because of the chicken-and-egg problem that comes up when the node currently starting is needed for quorum on the system config range. For example, if a three node cluster is completely down, at least two of the nodes must be online before current settings are received.

I think we should do two things here:

1. persist the settings locally on the first store, so that restarting nodes can come up with settings that are no staler than the ones they had when they went down.
2. if a new node joins the cluster, wait until it has gotten the settings from gossip (and applied them) before continuing to ready status.

Sorry, @irfansharif missed these comments.

I guess we might not want to block the refresh settings listener. Not entirely sure though. @tbg can weigh in here.

> We could consider returning the settings from the Join RPC (which replaces gossip-join), but let's hold off on that, at least in this PR, though it would be a good follow-up.

I assume this suggestion was motivated by not wanting to spend any time with stale settings? Instead of serializing settings through the Join RPC (which I think should stay simple - just node + cluster id + version, as it is today), perhaps what we could do here instead is wait for a gossip update containing the up-to-date settings. We'll want to do this after having joined the cluster, after having started up gossip, but before having fully started up the node. What do you think?
